summary: Okanogan County, WA tower built 1933, staffed from 1934, removed or destroyed in 1957; Willhite's 2020 account shows a foundation and woodpiles.

facts.design: Pole tower with L-6 cab, with a log cabin at the base
facts.status_note: Tower gone since 1957. Willhite's photos show a building foundation, footings and woodpiles.

access.note: Willhite says the left gate road is usually locked but was open during a timber sale; no source states a visiting rule

visit.trail_note: Gravel road to a gate 2 miles below the summit, then fallen trees across the road; no views remain

events.note: Pole tower with L-6 cab and a log cabin at the base
Mr. and Mrs. Vernon Wills of Tonasket
One tower leg found hollow with rot
Register says removed and never replaced; firelookout.com and Willhite say destroyed

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and firelookout.com give 65 feet (about 19.8 m). Willhite and the 1933 newspaper plan give 60 feet (18.3 m), the record's figure. Not resolved in facts.
The register says the tower was removed and never replaced; firelookout.com and Willhite say it was destroyed. All three put the end in 1957.

sources.title: Mount Annie Lookout Site, Former Fire Lookout Sites register
Mount Annie, Forest Lookouts (quotes Republic News-Miner and The Wenatchee Daily World)

notes_for_editor: Height is disputed (65 ft vs 60 ft); the record's 18.3 m is kept. Removal versus destruction in 1957 is disputed; both are in the events note. The access level was 'restricted', an inference from Willhite's note that the left gate is usually locked; no source states a visiting rule, so it is now 'unknown'. The 2020 visit is Willhite's; his photo captions are not individually dated.
